description: React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data

latest_release.body: - `List` identifies rows by `ariaAttributes` (specifically `aria-posinset`) so that additional children (e.g. sticky rows or overlays) aren't measured as rows, and rows that render nothing don't shift the indices of the rows after them. Rows that don't spread `ariaAttributes`, or that override `aria-posinset` or `aria-setsize`, are still matched by their position. If only some rows spread `ariaAttributes` (e.g. loaded rows but not loading placeholders), the rows that don't are not measured; spread `ariaAttributes` onto every row (or none). - [#930](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-window/pull/930), [#931](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-window/pull/931)

detail.readme:
`react-window` is a component library that helps render large lists of data quickly and without the performance problems that often go along with rendering a lot of data. It's used in a lot of places, from React DevTools to the Replay browser. ## Support If you like this project there are several ways to support it: - [Become a GitHub sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/bvaughn/) - [Become an Open Collective sponsor](https://opencollective.com/react-window#sponsor) - or [buy me a coffee](http://givebrian.coffee/) The following wonderful companies and individuals have sponsored react-window: ## Installation Begin by installing the library from NPM: ```sh npm install react-window ``` ## TypeScript types TypeScript definitions are included within the published `dist` folder ## FAQs Frequently asked questions can be found [here](https://react-window.vercel.app/common-questions). ## Documentation Documentation for this project is available at [react-window.vercel.app](https://react-window.vercel.app/). ## Components ### Grid Renders data with many rows and columns. ℹ️ Unlike `List` rows, `Grid` cell sizes must be known ahead of time. Either static sizes or something that can be derived (from the data in `CellProps`) without rendering. #### Required props
Name Description
cellComponent

React component responsible for rendering a cell.

This component will receive columnIndex, rowIndex, and style props by default. Additionally it will receive prop values passed to cellProps.

ℹ️ The prop types for this component are exported as CellComponentProps
cellProps

Additional props to be passed to the cell-rendering component. Grid will automatically re-render cells when values in this object change.

⚠️ This object must not contain ariaAttributes, columnIndex, rowIndex, or style props.
columnCount

Number of columns to be rendered in the grid.
columnWidth

Column width; the following formats are supported:

  • number of pixels (number)
  • percentage of the grid's current width (string)
  • function that returns the column width (in pixels) given an index and cellProps

ℹ️ Percentage widths can't be resolved during server rendering unless a defaultWidth (or a pixel width via the style prop) is specified.
rowCount

Number of rows to be rendered in the grid.
rowHeight

Row height; the following formats are supported:

  • number of pixels (number)
  • percentage of the grid's current height (string)
  • function that returns the row height (in pixels) given an index and cellProps

ℹ️ Percentage heights can't be resolved during server rendering unless a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) is specified.
#### Optional props
Name Description
className

CSS class name.
dir

Indicates the directionality of grid cells.

ℹ️ The directionality of an ancestor element can't be detected during server rendering; specify this prop explicitly for server-rendered right-to-left grids.

ℹ️ See HTML dir global attribute for more information.
style

Optional CSS properties. The grid of cells will fill the height and width defined by this style.
children

Additional content to be rendered within the grid (above cells). This property can be used to render things like overlays or tooltips.
columnKey

Grids use the column index as a key by default. This prop can be used along with the rowKey prop to provide a custom key value.

ℹ️ Custom keys can ensure better UX for sortable or filterable grids, particularly if your cell components are stateful. Refer to the React documentation for more info.

⚠️ This prop cannot be auto-memoized because it is called during render. It is important to always useCallback for this prop; do not use an inline function.
defaultHeight

Default height of grid (in pixels) for initial render, before its actual height has been measured.

ℹ️ Grids can't be measured during server rendering, so this value determines how many rows are server rendered. It's recommended to set this to the expected height of the grid (or to specify a pixel height via the style prop).
defaultScrollLeft

Initial horizontal scroll offset (in pixels) of the grid. This value is only applied once, when the grid first mounts with at least one column.

ℹ️ Server-rendered HTML can't be pre-scrolled, so server rendering always starts at the first column; the default scroll offset is applied once the grid hydrates.

⚠️ If the grid can't be scrolled that far when the offset is applied (e.g. it is hidden with display: none, or uses percentage column widths before its width has been measured), the offset is clamped or ignored and not retried. Specify a defaultWidth (or a pixel width via the style prop) when using percentage column widths.
defaultScrollTop

Initial vertical scroll offset (in pixels) of the grid. This value is only applied once, when the grid first mounts with at least one row.

ℹ️ Server-rendered HTML can't be pre-scrolled, so server rendering always starts at the first row; the default scroll offset is applied once the grid hydrates.

⚠️ If the grid can't be scrolled that far when the offset is applied (e.g. it is hidden with display: none, or uses percentage row heights before its height has been measured), the offset is clamped or ignored and not retried. Specify a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) when using percentage row heights.
defaultWidth

Default width of grid (in pixels) for initial render, before its actual width has been measured.

ℹ️ Grids can't be measured during server rendering, so this value determines how many columns are server rendered. It's recommended to set this to the expected width of the grid (or to specify a pixel width via the style prop).
gridRef

Imperative Grid API.

ℹ️ The useGridRef and useGridCallbackRef hooks are exported for convenience in TypeScript projects.
onCellsRendered

Callback notified when the range of rendered cells changes.
onResize

Callback notified when the Grid's outermost HTMLElement resizes. This may be used to (re)scroll a cell into view.
overscanCount

How many additional rows/columns to render outside of the visible area. This can reduce visual flickering near the edges of a grid when scrolling.
rowKey

Grids use the row index as a key by default. This prop can be used along with the columnKey prop to provide a custom key value.

ℹ️ Custom keys can ensure better UX for sortable or filterable grids, particularly if your cell components are stateful. Refer to the React documentation for more info.

⚠️ This prop cannot be auto-memoized because it is called during render. It is important to always useCallback for this prop; do not use an inline function.
scrollElement

Element that scrolls the grid, for grids that scroll along with other content (e.g. the page):

  • "window" to scroll with the page
  • an ancestor element that scrolls (e.g. stored with a useState ref callback); null until it has mounted

The grid renders at its full height and only renders the rows (and columns) visible within the scroll element's viewport. Its position within the scroll element is measured whenever it renders, scrolls, or resizes, and whenever content before it is resized, inserted, or removed (e.g. an image loading above the grid).

  • columns scroll with the scroll element too if the grid is as wide as its content (e.g. style={{ width: "max-content" }}); otherwise the grid fills the width of its parent and its columns scroll within it
  • scrollToCell, scrollToColumn and scrollToRow scroll whichever element scrolls each axis
  • defaultHeight and defaultWidth are used as the viewport size until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering)
  • percentage row heights and column widths are relative to the scroll element's viewport
  • defaultScrollLeft and defaultScrollTop are ignored

ℹ️ While the scroll element is null, the grid renders the first rows (as it does during server rendering).

⚠️ The grid's onScroll handler is only called when the grid scrolls its own columns; listen to the scroll element's "scroll" events instead (or use the useIsScrolling hook).
tagName

Can be used to override the root HTML element rendered by the Grid component. The default value is "div", meaning that Grid renders an HTMLDivElement as its root.

⚠️ In most use cases the default ARIA roles are sufficient and this prop is not needed.
### List Renders data with many rows. #### Required props
Name Description
rowComponent

React component responsible for rendering a row.

This component will receive an index and style prop by default. Additionally it will receive prop values passed to rowProps.

ℹ️ Spread ariaAttributes onto the row element; they identify it as a row (e.g. so that dynamic row heights are measured reliably)

ℹ️ The prop types for this component are exported as RowComponentProps
rowCount

Number of items to be rendered in the list.
rowHeight

Row height; the following formats are supported:

  • number of pixels (number)
  • percentage of the list's current height (string)
  • function that returns the row height (in pixels) given an index and rowProps
  • dynamic row height cache returned by the useDynamicRowHeight hook

ℹ️ Percentage heights can't be resolved during server rendering unless a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) is specified.

⚠️ Dynamic row heights are not as efficient as predetermined sizes. It's recommended to provide your own height values if they can be determined ahead of time.
rowProps

Additional props to be passed to the row-rendering component. List will automatically re-render rows when values in this object change.

⚠️ This object must not contain ariaAttributes, index, or style props.
#### Optional props
Name Description
className

CSS class name.
style

Optional CSS properties. The list of rows will fill the height defined by this style.
children

Additional content to be rendered within the list (above rows). This property can be used to render things like overlays or tooltips.
defaultHeight

Default height of list (in pixels) for initial render, before its actual height has been measured.

ℹ️ Lists can't be measured during server rendering, so this value determines how many rows are server rendered. It's recommended to set this to the expected height of the list (or to specify a pixel height via the style prop).
defaultScrollOffset

Initial scroll offset (in pixels) of the list. This value is only applied once, when the list first mounts with at least one row.

ℹ️ Server-rendered HTML can't be pre-scrolled, so server rendering always starts at the first row; the default scroll offset is applied once the list hydrates.

⚠️ If the list can't be scrolled that far when the offset is applied (e.g. it is hidden with display: none, or uses percentage row heights before its height has been measured), the offset is clamped or ignored and not retried. Specify a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) when using percentage row heights.
listRef

Ref used to interact with this component's imperative API.

This API has imperative methods for scrolling and a getter for the outermost DOM element.

ℹ️ The useListRef and useListCallbackRef hooks are exported for convenience in TypeScript projects.
onResize

Callback notified when the List's outermost HTMLElement resizes. This may be used to (re)scroll a row into view.
onRowsRendered

Callback notified when the range of visible rows changes.
overscanCount

How many additional rows to render outside of the visible area. This can reduce visual flickering near the edges of a list when scrolling.
rowKey

Lists use the row index as a key by default. This prop can provide a custom key value.

ℹ️ Custom keys can ensure better UX for sortable or filterable lists, particularly if your row components are stateful. Refer to the React documentation for more info.

⚠️ This prop cannot be auto-memoized because it is called during render. It is important to always useCallback for this prop; do not use an inline function.
scrollElement

Element that scrolls the list, for lists that scroll along with other content (e.g. the page):

  • "window" to scroll with the page
  • an ancestor element that scrolls (e.g. stored with a useState ref callback); null until it has mounted

The list renders at its full height and only renders the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport. Its position within the scroll element is measured whenever it renders, scrolls, or resizes, and whenever content before it is resized, inserted, or removed (e.g. an image loading above the list).

  • scrollToRow scrolls the scroll element
  • defaultHeight is used as the viewport height until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering)
  • percentage row heights are relative to the scroll element's viewport height
  • defaultScrollOffset is ignored

ℹ️ While the scroll element is null, the list renders the first rows (as it does during server rendering).

⚠️ The list itself doesn't scroll, so its onScroll handler isn't called; listen to the scroll element's "scroll" events instead (or use the useIsScrolling hook).
tagName

Can be used to override the root HTML element rendered by the List component. The default value is "div", meaning that List renders an HTMLDivElement as its root.

⚠️ In most use cases the default ARIA roles are sufficient and this prop is not needed.
## Hooks ### useDynamicRowHeight Creates a cache of measured row heights for lists whose rows can't be sized ahead of time. Pass the returned value as the `rowHeight` prop of `List` (or the `itemSize` option of `useVirtualizer`); rendered rows are then measured with a `ResizeObserver` and the list updates as their sizes change. Rows that have not yet been measured use the `defaultRowHeight` (or `initialRowHeights`, if provided). ℹ️ Dynamic row heights are more expensive than fixed sizes; prefer a number or function when row heights are known. #### Parameters
Name Description
defaultRowHeight

Estimated height (in pixels) of rows that have not yet been measured.
initialRowHeights?

Row heights (in pixels) that are known or can be estimated ahead of time, e.g. estimated from each row's content. This can be either an array (where each item is the height of the row at that index) or a Map of row index to height.

These values are used in place of defaultRowHeight until rows are rendered and measured, so providing them can make server-rendered lists and initial scroll positions more accurate.

ℹ️ This value is only read when the hook first mounts and when the key changes.
key?

Changing this value clears all measured row heights, e.g. when the list renders a different set of data.
### useGridCallbackRef Convenience hook to return a properly typed ref callback for the Grid component. Use this hook when you need to share the ref with another component or hook. ### useGridRef Convenience hook to return a properly typed ref for the Grid component. ### useIsScrolling Tracks whether an element (or the window) is currently scrolling, e.g. to render simplified content in place of rows that are expensive to render. Pass the element that scrolls: - a list or grid's own element (e.g. from `useListCallbackRef`) - "window" or the scroll element, for lists and grids that use the `scrollElement` prop Scrolling ends when the browser fires a "scrollend" event or, in browsers that don't support that event, after no scroll events have been received for `delay` milliseconds. ℹ️ Scrolling that starts and ends before React renders (e.g. an instant scroll) may not change this value. ⚠️ Changing this value re-renders any rows it is passed to (e.g. via `rowProps`) when scrolling starts and when it ends. #### Parameters
Name Description
target
delay?

Milliseconds without scroll events after which scrolling is considered to have ended (only used by browsers that don't support the "scrollend" event); defaults to 150.
### useListCallbackRef Convenience hook to return a properly typed ref callback for the List component. Use this hook when you need to share the ref with another component or hook. ### useListRef Convenience hook to return a properly typed ref for the List component. ### useVirtualizer Calculates which items to render, and where, for custom (headless) virtualized content (e.g. a `` or a custom layout). The returned items are positioned relative to the start of the element's content; how they are rendered (e.g. absolute positioning or spacer elements) is up to the caller. #### Parameters
Name Description
count

Number of items.
defaultScrollOffset?

Initial scroll offset (in pixels), applied once when the element first mounts with at least one item.

ℹ️ Ignored when a scrollElement is specified.
defaultSize?

Size (in pixels) of the viewport before it has been measured (e.g. during server rendering); this determines how many items are initially rendered.
dir?

Direction of horizontal content; detected from the element (or its ancestors) by default.
direction?

Direction that items are laid out in; defaults to "vertical".
element

Element that scrolls the items or, if a scrollElement is specified, the element that contains the items.

ℹ️ Item offsets are relative to the start of this element's content.
itemSize

Item size; the following formats are supported:

  • number of pixels (number)
  • percentage of the viewport's size (string)
  • function that returns the item size (in pixels) given an index
  • dynamic row height cache returned by the useDynamicRowHeight hook (vertical only); rendered items must be passed to measureElement and specify a data-index attribute

ℹ️ Sizes are cached until the value of this option changes; memoize functions (e.g. with useCallback) and only change them when sizes change.
onItemsRendered?

Callback notified when the range of visible (or rendered) items changes.
overscanCount?

How many additional items to render outside of the visible area; defaults to 3.
scrollElement?

Element that scrolls the items, for items that scroll along with other content (e.g. the page):

  • "window" to scroll with the page
  • an ancestor element that scrolls; null until it has mounted

See the scrollElement prop of List for more information.
## Imperative APIs ### GridImperativeAPI Ref used to interact with this component's imperative API. This API has imperative methods for scrolling and a getter for the outermost DOM element. ℹ️ The `useGridRef` and `useGridCallbackRef` hooks are exported for convenience in TypeScript projects. #### Methods
Name Description
scrollToCell

Scrolls the grid so that the specified row and column are visible. Like the browser's scrollIntoView, items are aligned within the CSS scroll-padding of the element being scrolled (e.g. scroll-padding-top can leave room for a sticky header).

  • behavior Determines whether scrolling is instant or animates smoothly
  • columnAlign Determines the horizontal alignment of the element within the grid
  • columnIndex Index of the column to scroll to (0-based)
  • rowAlign Determines the vertical alignment of the element within the grid
  • rowIndex Index of the row to scroll to (0-based)
scrollToColumn

Scrolls the grid so that the specified column is visible. Like the browser's scrollIntoView, items are aligned within the CSS scroll-padding of the element being scrolled (e.g. scroll-padding-top can leave room for a sticky header).

  • align Determines the horizontal alignment of the element within the grid
  • behavior Determines whether scrolling is instant or animates smoothly
  • index Index of the column to scroll to (0-based)
scrollToRow

Scrolls the grid so that the specified row is visible. Like the browser's scrollIntoView, items are aligned within the CSS scroll-padding of the element being scrolled (e.g. scroll-padding-top can leave room for a sticky header).

  • align Determines the vertical alignment of the element within the grid
  • behavior Determines whether scrolling is instant or animates smoothly
  • index Index of the row to scroll to (0-based)
### ListImperativeAPI Imperative List API. ℹ️ The `useListRef` and `useListCallbackRef` hooks are exported for convenience in TypeScript projects. #### Methods
Name Description
scrollToRow

Scrolls the list so that the specified row is visible. Like the browser's scrollIntoView, items are aligned within the CSS scroll-padding of the element being scrolled (e.g. scroll-padding-top can leave room for a sticky header). Dynamic row heights are measured after rendering; Content that resizes later may require another scrollToRow call.

ℹ️ For dynamic height lists, "smooth" scrolling is animated by the list (rather than the browser) so that the destination can be corrected as rows are measured along the way.

  • align Determines the vertical alignment of the element within the list
  • behavior Determines whether scrolling is instant or animates smoothly
  • index Index of the row to scroll to (0-based)
